descriptions.loop-review: Inspect a scoped change or repository and report prioritized findings with source evidence. Use for review; use loop-plan for planning, loop-evaluate for fixed-rubric scoring and loop-research workflows for adoption decisions.
descriptions.loop-code: Implement an authorized feature or configuration change in small verified batches. Prefer loop-debug when the main goal is repairing a reproducible bug and loop-refactor when the goal is restructuring without changing behavior.
descriptions.loop-diagnose: Investigate an unexplained symptom using competing hypotheses and discriminating experiments. Use for diagnosis without an assumed repair; prefer loop-debug for a requested fix, loop-diagnose-repro for minimization and the focused performance/regression routes when those are the goal.
descriptions.loop-diagnose-repro: Run a bounded reproduction loop for a bug or failure: capture the environment, minimize the reproducer, vary one factor at a time, and preserve exact evidence for a later fix.
descriptions.loop-diagnose-performance: Run a bounded performance-diagnosis loop for slow, memory-heavy, or resource-intensive behavior. Establish a baseline, profile safely, isolate a bottleneck, and verify a targeted improvement.
descriptions.loop-diagnose-regression: Run a bounded regression-diagnosis loop: compare a known-good and failing state, bisect or narrow the change set, reproduce the regression, and verify the smallest authorized fix.
descriptions.loop-research: Run a bounded evidence loop to research repositories, documentation, tools, extensions, plugins, skills, MCP servers, or implementation options. Use when the user asks to search, compare, or investigate repeatedly.
descriptions.loop-research-repo: Research repositories and open-source projects in a bounded evidence loop. Compare relevance, activity, license, security, compatibility, and maintenance before recommending adoption.
descriptions.loop-research-tools: Research tools, extensions, plugins, skills, and MCP servers in a bounded evidence loop. Evaluate capability, permissions, maintenance, compatibility, cost, and adoption risk before recommending or installing anything.
descriptions.loop-test: Select and execute a risk-based test strategy for a project or change when the required test layer is not yet known. Use focused unit, integration, E2E, coverage, adversarial or compatibility skills when that layer is already the main request.
descriptions.loop-test-unit: Run a bounded unit-test loop for a module or function: select focused tests, reproduce failures, improve authorized tests or fixtures, and verify isolated behavior without weakening acceptance criteria.
descriptions.loop-test-integration: Run a bounded integration-test loop across services, processes, files, databases, or external boundaries. Verify setup, contracts, failure paths, cleanup, and reproducibility.
descriptions.loop-test-coverage: Run a bounded test-coverage loop: identify untested risk, inspect coverage evidence, add authorized focused tests, and verify that coverage improvements are meaningful rather than cosmetic.
descriptions.loop-docs: Run a bounded documentation loop: audit README, guides, API references, examples, localization, and generated documentation; propose or make authorized updates; verify links and consistency. Use when the user asks to improve docs repeatedly.
descriptions.loop-skill-create: Create or maintain an agent skill through requirements, reusable-pattern inspection, synchronized editing, focused tests, documentation, and evidence review. Use when adding or changing a SKILL.md workflow.
descriptions.loop-orchestrate: Run bounded follow-up prompts through a configured headless coding-agent command with state, timeout, stop markers, and evidence. Use when a loop must continue in a new agent invocation.
descriptions.loop-prompt: Run an initial user prompt, have the agent infer the next useful prompt, and execute a bounded number of follow-up prompts with evidence. Use when the user requests /loop-prompt N.
descriptions.loop-debug: Repair a reproducible bug end to end: capture a failing test, isolate the cause, apply the smallest authorized fix, and rerun regression checks. Use when the user wants a bug fixed, rather than diagnosis alone.
descriptions.loop-security: Review authorized code and configuration for security risks using threat boundaries, source evidence and safe local tests. Use for a defensive security review or scoped remediation, not unrestricted probing.
descriptions.loop-refactor: Improve a scoped code structure while preserving observable behavior through characterization tests, small reversible changes and regression checks. Use for maintainability work without a feature or bug-fix behavior change.
descriptions.loop-ci: Diagnose and repair scoped CI failures by tracing a failed job to logs, reproducing locally where possible, and verifying workflow changes. Use for CI pipelines rather than general application debugging.
descriptions.loop-release: Prepare and verify a scoped release candidate: version consistency, reproducible build, package contents, changelog and rollback notes. Use for release readiness; publishing remains a separately authorized action.
descriptions.loop-plan: Turn a scoped request into dependency-ordered, verifiable implementation batches without changing code. Use before multi-step work when acceptance criteria, risks or sequencing need definition.
descriptions.loop-dependencies: Assess and perform an authorized dependency change with manifest/lockfile consistency, compatibility checks and rollback evidence. Use for project dependency maintenance rather than tool adoption.
descriptions.loop-migrate: Prepare and verify a scoped data, schema or configuration migration with dry-run, backup, invariants, idempotence and rollback. Use when stored state or format changes, not for behavior-preserving refactors.
descriptions.loop-test-e2e: Verify a complete user-visible journey through its real entry point, including success, invalid input and observable side effects. Use for end-to-end acceptance, not isolated units or one integration boundary.
descriptions.loop-evaluate: Evaluate a skill or agent workflow using predefined cases, an explicit rubric and independently checked outcomes. Use for quality measurement, false-positive analysis and baseline comparison rather than code coverage.
descriptions.loop-test-adversarial: Challenge a declared contract with isolated adversarial inputs and independently observed outcomes. Use to find false PASS results or boundary violations; use loop-security for a general threat review and loop-debug for an already identified bug.
descriptions.loop-test-compatibility: Verify a declared compatibility matrix across versions, platforms, host adapters or data formats. Use to distinguish structural portability from executed behavior; use loop-test-integration for one boundary and loop-test-e2e for one complete journey.
descriptions.loop-mcp-design: Design a scoped MCP client/server integration around a pinned protocol version, tool contracts and trust boundaries. Use before implementing or changing an MCP interface; use loop-mcp-test for execution and loop-mcp-security for defensive review.
descriptions.loop-mcp-test: Exercise a versioned MCP interface using bounded local fixtures or an explicitly authorized server. Check tool contracts, correlation, error behavior and side effects; use loop-test-integration for non-MCP boundaries and loop-mcp-design for planning.
descriptions.loop-mcp-security: Review an authorized MCP integration for tool trust, scoped authorization, credential handling and data-exfiltration boundaries. Use for MCP-specific defensive analysis; use loop-security for general code review and loop-test-adversarial for generic false-PASS challenges.
descriptions.loop-deploy: Execute or rehearse a scoped deployment of a known release with health gates and rollback evidence. Use after release preparation when environment rollout is the goal; use loop-ci for pipeline repair and loop-migrate for persisted-data transformations.
descriptions.loop-observe: Assess whether logs, metrics, traces and health signals can detect and explain an operational failure. Use for observability and alert verification; use loop-diagnose-performance for profiling and loop-deploy for executing a rollout.
descriptions.loop-context: Prepare a compact, source-linked context packet for a specific task from existing artifacts. Use to select relevant constraints and resolve stale context before implementation; use loop-research to discover new sources.
descriptions.loop-handoff: Create or validate a resumable checkpoint for unfinished agent work across sessions. Use to transfer current state, evidence and the next bounded action; use loop-orchestrate to launch follow-up processes.
descriptions.loop-workflow-project: Turn an authorized small-project idea into an incremental delivery workflow with an MVP boundary, acceptance backlog, first verified slice and resumable state. Use for a new project lifecycle, not a single code change.
descriptions.loop-workflow-pr: Prepare a reviewable pull-request delivery packet from a scoped branch or diff: establish the base, review changes, verify checks and write a truthful description. Create or update the remote PR only when authorized.
descriptions.loop-workflow-incident: Coordinate an active service-incident assessment: establish impact, separate observations from hypotheses, choose authorized containment and verify recovery. Use for operational disruption, not an ordinary reproducible development bug.
descriptions.loop-write: Draft or revise everyday emails, letters, announcements and short documents for a stated audience while preserving facts and intent. Use for communication writing, not technical repository documentation or sending messages.
descriptions.loop-summarize: Condense supplied documents, notes or transcripts into a source-grounded summary with traceable claims and unresolved contradictions. Use for faithful compression, not open-ended research or inventing a decision record.
descriptions.loop-meeting: Turn supplied meeting notes or transcripts into a traceable record of decisions, proposals, actions and open questions. Use for meeting follow-through, not generic summarization or automatically scheduling and messaging attendees.
descriptions.loop-organize: Plan or perform an explicitly authorized organization of local files or personal work items using an inventory, collision-safe mapping and reversible verification. Use for organizing existing material, not silent deletion, cloud migration or software refactoring.
descriptions.loop-decide: Compare everyday options against explicit priorities, costs, uncertainties and constraints, then give a conditional recommendation or decision record. Use for choosing among options, not inventing missing facts or making a high-stakes decision on the user's behalf.
descriptions.loop-learn: Build a realistic learning plan and practice session around a learner's goal, current level and available time, using retrieval, feedback and spaced review. Use for tutoring and study planning, not claiming mastery from a generated plan.

scope: One curated selection pass, not a general accuracy estimate.
